01 / WHERE IT BEGAN

Listen to the animal.
Share what you learn.

The company history traces MT E.L.K., INC. to Montana in 1985, with Don Laubach and Cow Talk at the center of its early story.

Mark Henckel’s October 1986 report from Gardiner, Montana, names Laubach and filmmaker Gordon Eastman in the company’s formation.

Read the 1986 Newspaper Record

02 / THROUGH THE YEARS

The call. The teaching.
The continuing story.

A timeline from company history and dated records. The indexed sources do not establish an ownership-transition date.

  1. 1985

    Montana beginnings

    The company’s archived history places MT E.L.K., INC.’s founding in Montana in 1985. The early business takes shape around Cow Talk and the experience behind it.

    SOURCE: PRESERVED COMPANY HISTORY
  2. 1986

    Cow Talk enters the newspaper record

    Mark Henckel’s October 10 feature in Helena’s Independent Record documents Laubach, Eastman, the call, early production, and the hunters using it.

    Read the newspaper feature
  3. 1988

    Field knowledge takes the public stage

    A March 24 Billings Gazette advertisement schedules Laubach’s elk-calling presentations at the Montana Outdoor Recreation Exposition on March 25–27. Other archived press coverage from the period documents books and instructional video alongside the calls.

    See the exposition record
  4. 1998

    A calling system—and a teaching tradition

    A July 30 company biographical sheet records Laubach’s calls, books with Mark Henckel, and video work with Gordon Eastman. Handwritten notes on the same sheet plan a store seminar and call demonstrations.

    Read the company biographical sheet
  5. CONTINUING
    STORY

    Carrying the story forward

    The preserved company history identifies T. Phillip Bowers as owner and steward of the MT E.L.K., INC. legacy. The continuing chapter connects that history with education, customer support, and the preservation of the records behind the story.

    Explore calling education →
